determination:
HEALTHFIRST HEALTH PLAN — APPEALS AND GRIEVANCES DIVISION
100 Medical Plaza Way, Suite 500
Los Angeles, CA 90024

Date: October 22, 2024

CASE ID: PA-2024-C002
MEMBER NAME: David Santos
MEMBER ID: M-101122
AGE: 63
PLAN: HealthFirst PPO Gold — Group Plan 77441
STATE: California
REQUESTED PROCEDURE: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C6-C7, One Level (CPT 22551)
REQUESTING PHYSICIAN: Dr. Lisa Wong, MD — Spine Surgery
FACILITY: Cedars-Sinai Medical Center
DENIAL DATE: October 5, 2024
DENIAL REVIEWER: Dr. Patricia Huang, MD

SUBJECT: APPEAL DETERMINATION — OVERTURN OF PRIOR AUTHORIZATION DENIAL

Dear Mr. Santos and Dr. Wong,

The HealthFirst Health Plan Appeals and Grievances Division has completed its de novo review of the first-level appeal regarding the prior authorization request for a one-level Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at C6-C7 (CPT code 22551) at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center. 

DISPOSITION: The initial denial issued on October 5, 2024, is hereby OVERTURNED. Prior authorization for CPT 22551 is APPROVED.

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The initial denial of prior authorization was based on a determination that the member's primary diagnosis was cervical radiculopathy rather than cervical myelopathy, thereby rendering the plan's "Myelopathy Exception" (Section 2.2) inapplicable and requiring the completion of standard conservative treatment. 

Upon de novo review of the complete clinical record as of the appeal date (October 20, 2024), this Division finds that the denial must be overturned on two independent grounds:
1. Standard Pathway Satisfaction: The member has fully completed and documented the failure of the plan's standard conservative treatment requirements under Section 2.2 of Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024. While the initial denial on October 5, 2024, was issued prematurely before the clinical outcome of the September 28, 2024, epidural steroid injection could be determined, the de novo appeal record now documents that the epidural failed to provide lasting relief after 3 weeks (fully returning to 8/10 pain by October 19, 2024).
2. Regulatory and Clinical Standard Alignment: Under California Health and Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.32 and Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) All-Plan Letter (APL) 22-014 Section II.3, the plan's internal criteria cannot be more restrictive than generally accepted standards of medical practice. Under the AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023 Update), the presence of myelomalacia (T2 cord signal change) on MRI is a Tier 1 Strong Indication for surgical intervention, making extended conservative trials clinically inappropriate. Furthermore, under California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(a)(3), the physical therapy requirement is legally waived due to objective evidence of structural neurological compromise.

II. CLINICAL PRESENTATION & RECORD REVIEW
The member is a 63-year-old male presenting with a mixed cervical myelopathy-radiculopathy.
- Objective Imaging: An MRI dated September 1, 2024, demonstrates C6-C7 moderate cord compression, T2 signal change (myelomalacia) within the spinal cord, and right C7 foraminal stenosis more prominent than the left.
- Neurological Examination: A physical exam dated September 5, 2024, reveals a mixed presentation. Radicular findings include predominant right C7 distribution tricep weakness (4/5) and right finger numbness, with pain rated at 8/10. Myelopathic findings include bilateral hyperreflexia (right > left), a positive right Hoffman sign, an equivocal left Hoffman sign, and a mildly wide-based gait.
- Conservative Treatment History:
  1. Physical Therapy: Completed 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy (18 sessions) utilizing a myelopathy protocol. The treating therapist documented no improvement in bilateral neurological signs or right-sided radicular symptoms.
  2. Pharmacotherapy: Completed a 3-month trial of Pregabalin 150mg BID (neuropathic agent) resulting in only partial right-sided pain relief, and a 2-month trial of Naproxen 500mg BID (NSAID) which was inadequate.
  3. Interventional Treatment: Received a right C7 cervical epidural steroid injection on September 28, 2024. The clinical record notes that the injection provided 50% temporary right-sided relief, but the pain fully returned to 8/10 within 3 weeks (by October 19, 2024), with no change in bilateral hyperreflexia.

III. PLAN CRITERIA ANALYSIS (CC-SPINE-2024)
Under HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2, surgical authorization for ACDF (CPT 22551) requires a confirmed diagnosis (Section 2.1), completion of conservative treatment (Section 2.2), and consistent imaging (Section 2.3).

1. Diagnosis and Imaging Requirements (Sections 2.1 & 2.3):
The member has a confirmed diagnosis of mixed cervical myelopathy-radiculopathy, satisfying both Section 2.1(a) (cervical radiculopathy) and Section 2.1(b) (cervical myelopathy). The MRI dated September 1, 2024, is within 6 months of the request and demonstrates structural pathology (moderate cord compression and myelomalacia at C6-C7) consistent with the member's symptoms, satisfying Section 2.3.

2. Standard Conservative Treatment Pathway (Section 2.2):
The initial denial on October 5, 2024, asserted that because radiculopathy was the primary diagnosis, the "Myelopathy Exception" (which modifies PT to 4 weeks and waives interventional treatment) did not apply, and standard conservative treatment was required. 

However, as of the de novo appeal review on October 20, 2024, the member has fully satisfied the standard conservative treatment requirements under Section 2.2:
- Section 2.2(a) (Physical Therapy): The member completed 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy (18 sessions), satisfying the standard 6-week requirement.
- Section 2.2(b) (Pharmacotherapy): The member completed a 3-month trial of Pregabalin (neuropathic agent) and a 2-month trial of Naproxen (NSAID). This satisfies the requirement for a trial of at least two qualifying agents for a minimum of 4 weeks each.
- Section 2.2(c) (Interventional Treatment): The member received a right C7 epidural steroid injection on September 28, 2024. At the time of the initial denial (October 5, 2024), only 7 days had elapsed, and the clinical outcome of the injection was pending. On de novo appeal review, we incorporate the documented clinical status as of October 19, 2024 (3 weeks post-injection), which confirms that the pain has fully returned to 8/10 and the interventional trial has failed. 

Because the member has completed and documented the failure of 6 weeks of PT, two qualifying medications for >4 weeks, and a cervical epidural steroid injection, the standard conservative treatment pathway is 100% satisfied. The plan's denial on the basis of incomplete conservative treatment is a misapplication of its own criteria.

IV. CALIFORNIA REGULATORY COMPLIANCE
1. California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(a)(3) — Physical Therapy Waiver:
CIC § 10169.5(a)(3) explicitly states that a health insurer shall not condition approval of a surgical procedure on the completion of physical therapy where the condition involves "objective evidence of structural neurological compromise that physical therapy cannot address." 
The member's MRI dated September 1, 2024, provides objective evidence of moderate cord compression and T2 signal change (myelomalacia), which represents structural neurological compromise. Therefore, the plan's 6-week physical therapy requirement (Section 2.2(a)) is legally waived and deemed satisfied under California law. 
While we explicitly acknowledge that CIC § 10169.5(a)(3) applies strictly to physical therapy and does not waive the plan's pharmacotherapy (Section 2.2(b)) or interventional (Section 2.2(c)) requirements, those requirements were independently and fully satisfied through the completed trials of Pregabalin, Naproxen, and the failed C7 epidural steroid injection.

2. DMHC All-Plan Letter (APL) 22-014 Section II.3 — Plan Criteria vs. Clinical Standard:
The initial denial relied on the "Note" in CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.2, which restricts the myelopathy exception to cases where myelopathy is the "primary diagnosis." 
We explicitly acknowledge that the conservative treatment waiver under APL 22-014 Section II.2(a) is inapplicable because it requires "progressive pathology... on serial imaging," and the clinical record contains only a single MRI from September 1, 2024. 
However, APL 22-014 Section II.3 mandates that plans "shall not apply internal criteria that are more restrictive than generally accepted standards of medical practice." Under CHSC § 1374.32(b), the standard of review for medical necessity is governed by generally accepted standards of medical practice, not a plan's restrictive internal criteria. As detailed below, generally accepted clinical standards do not restrict surgical indications based on whether myelopathy or radiculopathy is designated as "primary" when both are objectively present with myelomalacia. Therefore, the plan's "primary diagnosis" restriction is invalid under California regulatory standards, and the clinical standard must govern.

V. CLINICAL EVIDENCE & GENERALLY ACCEPTED STANDARDS
Under the AANS/CNS Joint Section on Disorders of the Spine Guidelines for the Management of Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy (2023 Update), surgical decompression is the standard of care for patients with moderate-to-severe myelopathy or those with objective structural cord compromise.
- Tier 1 Strong Indication: The guidelines classify "myelomalacia on MRI (cord signal change)" as a Tier 1 Strong Indication for surgical intervention (Section 3.1). 
- Clinical Inappropriateness of Delay: The clinical evidence base, including the AO Spine International Clinical Practice Guidelines (2021), demonstrates that there is no high-quality evidence supporting a mandatory course of conservative treatment prior to surgery for patients with objective cord compression and myelomalacia. Delaying surgery in these patients to complete extended conservative trials is associated with a high risk of irreversible neurological deterioration, as preoperative myelomalacia is the strongest predictor of incomplete neurological recovery (Section 2.3).
- Mixed Presentation: In clinical practice, cervical cord compression frequently coexists with nerve root compression (mixed myelopathy-radiculopathy). The presence of prominent radicular pain (8/10) and right-sided weakness does not negate the objective spinal cord injury (myelomalacia) and upper motor neuron signs (bilateral hyperreflexia, positive Hoffman sign, wide-based gait). Under generally accepted clinical standards, any presence of myelomalacia is a critical clinical indicator that makes extended conservative trials inappropriate, regardless of which symptom is subjectively labeled as "primary."

VI. CONCLUSION
The member, David Santos, has a mixed cervical myelopathy-radiculopathy with objective MRI evidence of C6-C7 moderate cord compression and myelomalacia. 
1. Under a de novo review of the clinical record as of October 20, 2024, the member has fully completed and failed the plan's standard conservative treatment pathway (6 weeks PT, 3 months Pregabalin, 2 months Naproxen, and a failed C7 epidural steroid injection), satisfying Section 2.2 of CC-SPINE-2024.
2. Under California Insurance Code § 10169.5(a)(3), the physical therapy requirement is legally waived due to objective structural neurological compromise.
3. Under DMHC APL 22-014 Section II.3, the plan's internal restriction requiring myelopathy to be the "primary diagnosis" is impermissibly more restrictive than generally accepted clinical standards (AANS/CNS 2023 Guidelines), which recommend immediate surgical decompression for patients with documented myelomalacia.

Accordingly, the prior authorization denial for ACDF C6-C7 (CPT 22551) is OVERTURNED, and the procedure is APPROVED.

Sincerely,

Appeals and Grievances Division
HealthFirst Health Plan
ground_truth_answer: OVERTURN — CIC 10169.5(a)(3) applies based on documented myelomalacia. The regulatory provision does not require myelopathy to be the primary diagnosis — it requires objective evidence of structural neurological compromise. Myelomalacia is such evidence. The primary diagnosis restriction in the plan's exception clause cannot override the statutory prohibition.
genuine_tension: The plan acknowledges myelopathy exists but argues it is secondary to radiculopathy. For the plan criteria myelopathy exception, the plan may have a defensible argument. But CIC 10169.5(a)(3) does not ask which diagnosis is primary — it asks whether objective evidence of structural neurological compromise that physical therapy cannot address is present. Myelomalacia on MRI is exactly that, regardless of whether radiculopathy is also present.

determination:
**APPEAL DETERMINATION: PA-2024-D001**

**Member:** Sandra White (M-334466)
**Procedure:** ACDF C6-C7, one level (CPT 22551)
**Date of Initial Denial:** 2024-10-05

**DISPOSITION: OVERTURNED**

**WARRANT:**

This appeal determination is based on a comprehensive review of the provided case information, the HealthFirst PPO Gold plan criteria (CC-SPINE-2024), relevant California state laws and regulations, and generally accepted clinical standards. The review adheres to the established hierarchy of authority: State Law > Clinical Standard > Plan Criteria.

**1. Procedural Adequacy of Denial Notice (State Law Review):**
The appeal basis highlights significant procedural defects in the initial denial notice.
*   **CHSC 1374.31(b) mandates that a denial notice SHALL:**
    *   Specify the exact clinical criteria applied.
    *   Include the specific clinical reason for the denial.
    *   Provide notice of the member's right to Independent Medical Review (IMR).
*   **Case Findings:** The initial denial notice explicitly states "Generic reference to plan criteria — no section number, no specific criterion" and "imr_notice_included: false."
*   **Conclusion:** The denial notice is procedurally defective, as it fails to meet the clear requirements of California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(b). A denial notice that fails to specify the clinical criteria applied or the specific clinical reason for the denial is to be treated as if no denial was issued. This procedural defect alone is sufficient grounds to **OVERTURN** the denial.

**2. Clinical Presentation and Applicability of Myelopathy Exceptions:**
Before addressing the substantive denial reason, it is critical to accurately classify the member's condition.
*   **Clinical Record Findings:**
    *   **Presenting Diagnosis:** Cervical radiculopathy C6-C7.
    *   **Imaging (MRI):** C6-C7 disc herniation, moderate right C7 nerve root compression. **Crucially, there is no cord contact and no myelomalacia documented.**
    *   **Neurological Exam:** Right C7 dermatomal numbness, tricep weakness 4/5 right, tricep reflex diminished. These are classic signs of radiculopathy, not myelopathy (which would typically involve upper motor neuron signs like hyperreflexia, Hoffman's sign, gait disturbance, and often bilateral symptoms).
*   **Domain Knowledge and Clinical Standard (AANS/CNS 2023, AO Spine 2021):** Clearly distinguishes radiculopathy from myelopathy. Myelopathy involves spinal cord compression, often with upper motor neuron signs and potentially myelomalacia (cord signal change). Radiculopathy involves nerve root compression.
*   **Plan Criteria (HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.2(A) Exception):** The myelopathy pathway for reduced conservative treatment (4 weeks PT, waived interventional) explicitly states it "applies only when myelopathy is the PRIMARY diagnosis."
*   **State Law (DMHC APL 22-014):** This All-Plan Letter, which allows for waiver of conservative treatment, is specifically for "time-sensitive neurological conditions" like myelopathy with objective evidence of cord compression and myelomalacia.
*   **Conclusion:** Based on the clinical evidence (no cord contact, no myelomalacia, and neurological findings consistent with nerve root compression rather than spinal cord compression), the member's primary diagnosis is cervical radiculopathy. Therefore, neither the plan's myelopathy exception nor the state law provisions regarding urgent myelopathy with myelomalacia apply to this case.

**3. Substantive Review of Conservative Treatment (Plan Criteria & Clinical Standard):**
The plan's denial was based on incomplete conservative treatment. We assess this against plan criteria and clinical standards for *radiculopathy*.
*   **HealthFirst Plan Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.2):**
    *   (a) **Physical therapy:** Requires a minimum of 6 weeks. Member completed 4 weeks (12 sessions). **CRITERION NOT MET.**
    *   (b) **Pharmacotherapy:** Requires a trial of at least two agents for a minimum of 4 weeks each. Member tried Ibuprofen 800mg TID for 6 weeks (one agent). **CRITERION NOT MET.**
    *   (c) **Interventional treatment:** Requires one interventional treatment. Member had none. **CRITERION NOT MET.**
*   **California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5 (Physical Therapy as Prerequisite):**
    *   This law prohibits conditioning surgery on PT completion if: (1) PT is contraindicated/unlikely to benefit, OR (2) member reached a functional plateau, OR (3) there's objective evidence of structural neurological compromise that PT cannot address.
    *   **Case Findings:** There is no documentation that PT is contraindicated or unlikely to benefit. While the member claims a functional plateau, the PT discharge note does not use that language, and the structured fields do not provide sufficient detail to definitively meet the clinical definition of a functional plateau (<10% improvement over 3 sessions or therapist documentation of maximum benefit). As established, there is no objective evidence of structural neurological compromise (like myelomalacia or cord contact) that PT cannot address.
    *   **Conclusion:** The available documentation does not conclusively meet the criteria in CIC § 10169.5 to waive the plan's PT duration requirement.
*   **Clinical Standard (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020):** For cervical radiculopathy, surgery is typically indicated for "persistent symptoms after 6-12 weeks conservative tx" (Tier 2). The evidence base for conservative treatment is strong for radiculopathy. Generally accepted standards for managing radiculopathy include a trial of physical therapy (often 6-12 weeks), multiple pharmacotherapy agents, and often interventional procedures (e.g., epidural steroid injections).
*   **Conclusion:** The member's conservative treatment regimen (4 weeks of PT, one pharmacotherapy agent, no interventional procedures) is incomplete when compared to both HealthFirst's plan criteria for radiculopathy and generally accepted clinical standards for the management of cervical radiculopathy. The plan's criteria for conservative treatment in radiculopathy cases (6 weeks PT, 2 pharmacotherapies, 1 interventional) are consistent with, and not more restrictive than, generally accepted standards of medical practice.

**Summary and Final Determination:**

The initial denial by HealthFirst Health Plan (PA-2024-D001) is procedurally defective because it violates California Health & Safety Code § 1374.31(b) by failing to specify the clinical criteria applied and not including the Independent Medical Review notice. State law is the highest authority in the review hierarchy. Therefore, the denial cannot be upheld.

However, it is also important to note for future consideration that a substantive review of the clinical record against both the plan's criteria and generally accepted clinical standards for cervical radiculopathy reveals that the member's conservative treatment regimen is incomplete. The member's condition is consistent with cervical radiculopathy, not myelopathy, and therefore the specific state law and plan exceptions related to myelopathy or myelomalacia do not apply.

Given the mandatory nature of CHSC § 1374.31(b), the denial must be **OVERTURNED** due to its procedural inadequacy. HealthFirst Health Plan is advised to process the prior authorization request in a manner compliant with CHSC § 1374.31(b) if further review or a new denial is deemed necessary.

**Expert Reviewer:** [Your Name/Title - Expert Health Plan Appeals Reviewer]
**Date:** [Current Date]
ground_truth_answer: REMAND — The clinical denial is substantively correct (criteria not met: 4 weeks PT vs 6 required, one pharmacotherapy agent, no injection). However, the denial notice violates CHSC 1374.31(b): no specific criteria cited, no section number, no IMR notice. The plan must reissue a compliant denial notice before the member can meaningfully exercise appeal rights.
genuine_tension: Clinical criteria clearly not met — this is a legitimate denial on the merits. But the denial notice violates CHSC 1374.31(b) on multiple grounds. A single-pass system reads the clinical record and upholds. A system applying the full regulatory framework catches the procedural defect. The correct disposition is not a binary overturn/uphold — it is a remand requiring a compliant denial notice.

determination:
HEALTHFIRST HEALTH PLAN — APPEALS AND GRIEVANCES DIVISION
INDEPENDENT CLINICAL DETERMINATION

Date: December 10, 2024
Case ID: PA-2024-C003
Member Name: Helen Brooks
Member ID: M-112244
Plan: HealthFirst PPO Gold — Group Plan 77441
Requested Procedure: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C4-C5, one level (CPT 22551)
Requested By: Dr. James Park, MD — Neurosurgery
Facility: UCSF Medical Center
Appeal Date: December 5, 2024
Original Denial Date: November 20, 2024
Reviewer: Appeals Clinical Review Committee

FINAL DISPOSITION: OVERTURN (Full Prior Authorization Approved)

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Appeals and Grievances Division of HealthFirst Health Plan has completed its review of the first-level internal appeal filed on behalf of Helen Brooks regarding the prior authorization denial for a one-level Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at C4-C5 (CPT 22551). The initial denial issued on November 20, 2024, by Dr. Alan Foster, MD, is hereby OVERTURNED. 

A final, binary determination of OVERTURN is issued. Under California Health and Safety Code (CHSC) § 1367.01 and § 1374.31, the health plan's internal appeals division must issue a final, binary determination (Overturn or Uphold). A plan cannot "remand" its own appeal to the state-run Independent Medical Review (IMR) process; doing so would constitute a procedural failure to issue a timely decision, resulting in an automatic "deemed approved" status under CHSC § 1367.01 and California Code of Regulations (CCR) Title 28 § 1300.67.2.1.

Furthermore, delaying surgical authorization for this patient violates Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) All-Plan Letter (APL) 22-014, which classifies cervical myelopathy with objective cord compression and myelomalacia as an urgent condition with potential for irreversible neurological harm if untreated. Immediate surgical authorization is hereby granted to comply with state regulatory mandates and prevent progressive, irreversible spinal cord injury.

II. CLINICAL PRESENTATION AND RECORD REVIEW
The clinical record establishes the following objective findings:
1. Clinical Presentation: The patient is a 49-year-old female presenting with early cervical myelopathy. A comprehensive neurological examination on October 5, 2024, documented significant upper motor neuron (UMN) signs, including bilateral Hoffman signs, bilateral hyperreflexia of the upper extremities, and subtle balance impairment on tandem gait.
2. Imaging Findings: 
   - An MRI of the cervical spine dated October 1, 2024 (interpreted by Radiologist A), demonstrated a C4-C5 disc herniation with cord contact and noted a "possible early T2 signal change — equivocal, may represent artifact. Clinical correlation required."
   - A second read of the same MRI on October 15, 2024, by Radiologist B at the treating hospital (UCSF Medical Center), confirmed "C4-C5 cord compression with early myelomalacia." Radiologist B explicitly documented that the "T2 hyperintensity is reproducible on multiple sequences and represents early cord signal change, not artifact," which is highly consistent with early myelopathy.
   - On November 5, 2024, the plan's imaging reviewer (Dr. Alan Foster, MD) disputed these findings, asserting that the T2 signal change was "below threshold for clinical significance" and represented "artifact or normal variant."
3. Conservative Treatment:
   - Physical Therapy: The patient completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (24 sessions) directed at her cervical spine, with documented failure to improve her upper motor neuron signs.
   - Pharmacotherapy: The patient completed a 3-month trial of Gabapentin (400mg TID) with partial benefit, and a 6-week trial of Cyclobenzaprine with minimal response.
   - Interventional Treatment: No interventional procedures (such as epidural steroid injections) were performed. Dr. James Park, MD (Neurosurgery), explicitly documented that a referral for an epidural steroid injection was withheld because epidural steroid injections are relatively contraindicated in the presence of severe spinal cord compression due to the risk of acute neurological deterioration.

III. RESOLUTION OF RADIOLOGICAL CONFLICT UNDER CALIFORNIA LAW AND CLINICAL STANDARDS
The initial denial was based on the plan radiologist's assertion that the T2 signal change was an artifact and below the threshold of clinical significance. To reach a final binary determination, this conflict must be resolved using the established regulatory hierarchy: California State Law > Generally Accepted Clinical Standards > Plan's Internal Criteria.

1. Standard of Review under California Law (CHSC § 1374.32):
Under CHSC § 1374.32(a), medical necessity must be determined in accordance with "generally accepted standards of medical practice." Generally accepted clinical standards (AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines 2023; NASS Guidelines 2020; AO Spine Guidelines 2021) dictate that when a qualified radiologist at a treating academic medical center (UCSF) identifies reproducible T2 hyperintensity on multiple sequences representing early myelomalacia, and this finding is clinically correlated with objective upper motor neuron signs (bilateral Hoffman signs, hyperreflexia, and gait impairment), the diagnosis of cervical myelopathy is established. A remote plan reviewer's unilateral re-interpretation of the imaging as "artifact" to deny surgery is inconsistent with prudent clinical judgment and generally accepted medical standards. Therefore, the treating hospital's radiological interpretation controls.

2. Urgency and Risk of Delay (DMHC APL 22-014):
DMHC All-Plan Letter APL 22-014 (Section II.1) mandates that cervical myelopathy with objective evidence of cord compression and myelomalacia on MRI constitutes a condition with potential for irreversible harm if untreated. Plans are prohibited from applying restrictive internal criteria that delay treatment for such time-sensitive neurological conditions. Delaying surgery to resolve a radiological dispute or to enforce standard conservative pathways violates APL 22-014 and exposes the patient to progressive, irreversible spinal cord injury (e.g., worsening gait or hand weakness).

3. Statutory Override of Conservative Treatment (CIC § 10169.5):
Under California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(a)(3), a health plan is prohibited from conditioning approval of a surgical procedure on the completion of physical therapy when the patient's condition involves "objective evidence of structural neurological compromise that physical therapy cannot address." The patient's MRI demonstrates objective structural spinal cord compression and myelomalacia, which are structural lesions that physical therapy cannot mechanically resolve. Insisting on further conservative therapy in the face of active spinal cord injury violates CIC § 10169.5, rendering any further physical therapy requirements legally moot.

IV. COMPLIANCE WITH PLAN CRITERIA (CC-SPINE-2024)
Even under the plan's own internal clinical coverage guidelines (CC-SPINE-2024), the patient fully satisfies the criteria for surgical authorization under Section 2.2(A) — Myelopathy Pathway (Myelopathy Exception):
1. Diagnosis Requirement (Section 2.1(b)): The patient has a confirmed diagnosis of cervical myelopathy, supported by objective clinical findings (bilateral Hoffman signs, bilateral hyperreflexia, and tandem gait impairment) and current MRI imaging demonstrating C4-C5 cord compression and myelomalacia.
2. Modified Conservative Treatment (Section 2.2(A)):
   - Physical Therapy: The Myelopathy Exception reduces the physical therapy requirement to a minimum of 4 weeks. The patient completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (exceeding the requirement) and reached a functional plateau with no improvement in her upper motor neuron signs.
   - Pharmacotherapy: The patient completed trials of two qualifying agents (Gabapentin for 3 months and Cyclobenzaprine for 6 weeks), satisfying Section 2.2(b).
   - Interventional Treatment Waiver: Section 2.2(A) explicitly states that the interventional treatment requirement (2.2(c)) is WAIVED if the treating physician documents that interventional treatment poses a risk of neurological deterioration. Dr. James Park, MD, documented that epidural steroid injections are relatively contraindicated due to the patient's spinal cord compression and the risk of acute neurological decline. The interventional requirement is therefore fully waived.

Because the patient satisfies all elements of the Myelopathy Exception 2.2(A), the plan's initial denial was an arbitrary misapplication of its own clinical guidelines, constituting a bad-faith denial of benefits.

V. CONCLUSION AND AUTHORIZATION
Applying the regulatory hierarchy and clinical standards, the radiological conflict is resolved in favor of the treating hospital's radiologist and neurosurgeon. The patient has confirmed cervical myelopathy with early myelomalacia and correlating upper motor neuron signs, representing an urgent neurological condition under DMHC APL 22-014. The patient has met all applicable plan criteria under the CC-SPINE-2024 Myelopathy Exception, and further conservative treatment is legally barred from being used as a barrier to approval under CIC § 10169.5(a)(3).

The prior authorization denial for CPT 22551 (ACDF C4-C5, one level) is OVERTURNED. Immediate approval is issued.

Authorization Details:
- Approved Procedure: CPT 22551 (ACDF C4-C5, one level)
- Facility: UCSF Medical Center
- Provider: Dr. James Park, MD
- Authorization Period: 90 days from the date of this letter (valid through March 10, 2025)

This is a final determination of the HealthFirst Health Plan Appeals and Grievances Division.
ground_truth_answer: GATE / REMAND — Conflicting qualified radiologist interpretations of the same MRI create genuine uncertainty requiring physician review. The plan cannot simply rely on its own radiologist when the treating institution's radiologist reached a different conclusion on the same image. This case should be remanded for Independent Medical Review under CHSC 1374.30. A binary OVERTURN or UPHOLD without acknowledging the radiological conflict is wrong.
genuine_tension: Conflicting radiologist readings on the same imaging. Plan's radiologist says no myelomalacia. Treating radiologist says early myelomalacia. Clinical exam shows UMN signs. The plan denied based on its own radiologist's interpretation. Under CHSC 1374.32, the plan must use generally accepted medical standards — when qualified radiologists disagree, does the plan get to use its own reviewer's interpretation to deny?

determination:
# INDEPENDENT MEDICAL APPEAL DETERMINATION

**CASE ID:** PA-2024-D001  
**MEMBER:** Sandra White (ID: M-334466)  
**AGE:** 44  
**PLAN:** HealthFirst PPO Gold — Group Plan 77441  
**STATE OF JURISDICTION:** California  
**PLAN YEAR:** 2024  
**COVERAGE EFFECTIVE DATE:** November 1, 2020  
**DISPUTED SERVICE:** CPT Code 22551 (Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion [ACDF], C6-C7, single level)  
**REQUESTING CLINICIAN:** Dr. Paul Lee, MD — Neurosurgery (UCLA Medical Center)  
**DETERMINATION DATE:** October 28, 2024  

---

### I. FORMAL DISPOSITION

The clinical denial of prior authorization for CPT Code 22551 (ACDF C6-C7) is hereby **UPHELD**. 

**ADMINISTRATIVE FINDING:** HealthFirst Health Plan is found to be in **PROXIMATE PROCEDURAL VIOLATION** of California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(b) for issuing a defective denial notice. 

While the plan’s initial denial notice was administratively and legally defective, a procedural violation cannot legally or clinically mandate the approval of an invasive surgical procedure that is not medically necessary. Under generally accepted clinical standards (CHSC § 1374.32(b)) and the governing Hierarchy of Authority, the requested ACDF is not medically necessary at this time because the member has a stable, non-emergent cervical radiculopathy and has not completed an adequate trial of conservative management.

---

### II. HIERARCHY OF AUTHORITY
To resolve conflicts between clinical guidelines, plan policies, and state mandates, the following hierarchy of authority has been applied sequentially:
$$\text{California State Law \& Regulatory Mandates (CIC, CHSC, DMHC APL)} > \text{Generally Accepted Clinical Standards (AANS/CNS, AO Spine, NASS)} > \text{Plan Internal Criteria (HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024)}$$

---

### III. STEP-BY-STEP EVALUATION

#### STEP 1: Procedural Adequacy & Compliance Review
*   **Authority:** California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(b).
*   **Analysis:** Review of the initial denial notice dated October 5, 2024, issued by Dr. Alan Foster, MD, reveals major omissions:
    1.  The notice contains only a generic, boilerplate reference to "plan criteria" without citing the specific clinical policy name, section number, or exact criteria applied.
    2.  The notice fails to include the mandatory, state-regulated Independent Medical Review (IMR) notification.
*   **Finding (Negative):** The denial notice is **defective** under CHSC § 1374.31(b). A denial notice that fails to specify the clinical criteria applied or fails to include the mandatory state-regulated IMR notice constitutes a fatal procedural defect. Under state law, this must be treated as an administrative failure and documented as a primary basis of appeal. However, because performing unnecessary spinal fusion risks patient harm, this administrative defect does not bypass a rigorous review of clinical necessity. The review must proceed to Step 2.

#### STEP 2: Diagnostic Classification and Severity Assessment
*   **Authority:** Clinical Standards (AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines 2023, AO Spine Clinical Practice Guidelines 2021); HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.1.
*   **Analysis:** 
    *   *Imaging:* The MRI dated August 15, 2024, demonstrates "C6-C7 disc herniation, moderate right C7 nerve root compression." Crucially, the radiologist notes: **"No cord contact. No myelomalacia."**
    *   *Neurological Exam:* Dr. Paul Lee's physical exam on August 20, 2024, documents "Right C7 dermatomal numbness, tricep weakness 4/5 right, tricep reflex diminished." These are unilateral, lower motor neuron findings matching a C7 nerve root distribution. There are no bilateral upper extremity deficits, no upper motor neuron signs (e.g., hyperreflexia, clonus, positive Hoffman sign), and no gait instability.
*   **Finding (Negative):** The clinical record does not support a diagnosis of cervical myelopathy (which requires objective spinal cord compression, upper motor neuron signs, and/or cord signal changes/myelomalacia). Instead, the clinical presentation and objective imaging are classified as **Cervical Radiculopathy** under Section 2.1(a). The standard Radiculopathy clinical pathway must be applied.

#### STEP 3: Application of Plan-Specific Criteria and Internal Exceptions
*   **Authority:** HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.2.
*   **Analysis:** For a primary diagnosis of Cervical Radiculopathy, the member must satisfy the standard conservative treatment requirements under Section 2.2:
    1.  *Physical Therapy (Section 2.2(a)):* Requires a minimum of 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy with documented functional outcomes. *The member has completed only 4 weeks (12 sessions).* While the member self-reported a functional plateau, the physical therapy discharge summary does not support this language or document a clinical plateau.
    2.  *Pharmacotherapy (Section 2.2(b)):* Requires a trial of at least two classes of agents for a minimum of 4 weeks each. *The member has trialed only one agent* (Ibuprofen 800mg TID for 6 weeks, providing partial relief).
    3.  *Interventional Treatment (Section 2.2(c)):* Requires at least one interventional procedure (e.g., cervical epidural steroid injection). *The member has completed zero interventional procedures.*
    4.  *Exception 2.2(A) (Myelopathy Pathway):* This exception, which reduces the PT requirement to 4 weeks and waives the interventional treatment requirement, does *not* apply because the member's primary diagnosis is radiculopathy without cord compression or myelopathy.
*   **Finding (Negative):** The member has not completed the standard conservative treatment trials required under HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.2.

#### STEP 4: Statutory and Regulatory Override Assessment
*   **Authority:** California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5; DMHC All-Plan Letter (APL) 22-014.
*   **Analysis:** We must evaluate whether state mandates override the plan's conservative therapy requirements:
    *   *CIC § 10169.5(a)(1):* The treating physician has not documented in writing that PT is contraindicated or unlikely to benefit the member.
    *   *CIC § 10169.5(a)(2):* There is no provider-documented "functional plateau" (defined as a documented failure to achieve meaningful functional improvement after a course of therapy, as determined by the therapist or physician).
    *   *CIC § 10169.5(a)(3) & DMHC APL 22-014:* These provisions prohibit plans from requiring conservative therapy completion when there is objective evidence of structural neurological compromise that PT cannot address, or progressive pathology. Under APL 22-014, the presence of **myelomalacia** or severe cord compression on MRI specifically supports a waiver of conservative trials. However, the member's MRI explicitly rules out cord contact and myelomalacia, demonstrating stable, moderate nerve root compression.
*   **Finding (Negative):** The statutory and regulatory overrides under CIC § 10169.5 and DMHC APL 22-014 do not apply. The plan's conservative therapy requirements are legally valid in this clinical scenario.

#### STEP 5: Clinical Standards Conformity Review
*   **Authority:** CHSC § 1374.32(b); AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023); AO Spine Clinical Practice Guidelines (2021).
*   **Analysis:** Under CHSC § 1374.32(b), the standard of medical necessity must align with generally accepted standards of medical practice, which override plan-specific policies if those policies are more restrictive.
    *   According to the **AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023)**, a 1-level ACDF for cervical radiculopathy is a Tier 2 "reasonable option" only after a failed course of 6 to 12 weeks of conservative therapy. Proceeding directly to major spinal fusion after only 4 weeks of physical therapy and a single NSAID trial, with no interventional therapy trials and no progressive neurological deficit, does *not* meet generally accepted standards of medical practice.
    *   **AO Spine (2021)** and **NASS (2020)** guidelines support an initial 6-to-12-week trial of conservative therapies for stable radiculopathy. Because 70% to 80% of cervical radiculopathy cases resolve non-operatively, exposing a patient to the risks of a cervical fusion (such as adjacent segment disease, pseudarthrosis, and dysphagia) without completing an adequate conservative trial is clinically inappropriate.
*   **Finding (Negative):** The requested procedure does not meet generally accepted clinical standards of medical necessity at this time.

---

### IV. CLINICAL RATIONALE & DISCUSSION

This case represents a clinical scenario where the member has a clear, objectively confirmed diagnosis of **Cervical Radiculopathy** at the C6-C7 level. The member's symptoms (unilateral C7 dermatomal numbness, 4/5 tricep weakness, and diminished tricep reflex) correlate with the August 15, 2024 MRI findings of moderate right C7 nerve root compression. 

However, there is no clinical or radiographic evidence of **Cervical Myelopathy**. The spinal cord itself is entirely free of compression ("no cord contact"), and there is no spinal cord injury or signal change ("no myelomalacia"). 

For stable, non-emergent cervical radiculopathy, both HealthFirst plan criteria and national neurosurgical standards (AANS/CNS, NASS, AO Spine) require an adequate trial of conservative management prior to electing a major surgical fusion. This trial is designed to prevent unnecessary surgery, as the majority of radiculopathies resolve with non-operative care. 

The member has only completed **4 weeks of physical therapy**, trialed only **one medication class** (Ibuprofen), and has had **no interventional trials** (such as a cervical epidural steroid injection). While the member self-reported a "functional plateau," this is not documented in the physical therapy discharge summary or by the treating neurosurgeon, and does not meet the legal definition of a functional plateau under CIC § 10169.5(b). 

Because there is no progressive neurological deficit, cord compression, or myelomalacia, there is no medical justification to bypass the remaining conservative therapy trials. Therefore, the request for CPT 22551 is clinically premature and is not medically necessary.

---

### V. MANDATED CORRECTIVE INSTRUCTIONS TO THE PLAN

Although the surgical denial is upheld on clinical grounds, HealthFirst Health Plan is in violation of California statutory requirements regarding the execution of prior authorization reviews. 

Under **California Health & Safety Code § 1374.31(b)**, HealthFirst is **ORDERED** to immediately correct its denial notification practices. For all future medical necessity denials, the plan must:
1.  **Specify the exact clinical criteria applied**, including the specific clinical policy name (e.g., CC-SPINE-2024), section number, and subsection.
2.  **Provide the specific clinical reason** why the member failed to meet those criteria, detailing the specific clinical documentation that was lacking.
3.  **Include the mandatory Independent Medical Review (IMR) notification** and application forms as required by California law.

---

### VI. PATHWAY TO APPROVAL FOR MEMBER

To establish the medical necessity of CPT Code 22551 (ACDF C6-C7) upon future re-submission, the member and Dr. Paul Lee should complete the following conservative treatment steps:

1.  **Complete Physical Therapy:** Complete an additional 2 weeks of supervised, directed cervical physical therapy to satisfy the standard 6-week clinical trial requirement. If the member cannot complete this due to severe pain, the physical therapist or Dr. Lee must explicitly document a "functional plateau" (<10% clinical improvement over 3 consecutive sessions) or document that PT is clinically contraindicated.
2.  **Trial a Second Class of Pharmacotherapy:** Attempt a 4-week trial of a second pharmacotherapy agent (e.g., a muscle relaxant like cyclobenzaprine, or a neuropathic agent like gabapentin or pregabalin) as required by Section 2.2(b).
3.  **Interventional Consultation:** Undergo at least one cervical epidural steroid injection (or provide documented clinical justification from Dr. Lee explaining why an injection poses an unacceptable risk of neurological deterioration).

If the member's symptoms fail to improve after these steps, or if she experiences a documented progressive motor deficit (e.g., worsening tricep weakness below 4/5), a re-submitted request for ACDF should be approved immediately.
ground_truth_answer: REMAND — The clinical denial is substantively correct (criteria not met: 4 weeks PT vs 6 required, one pharmacotherapy agent, no injection). However, the denial notice violates CHSC 1374.31(b): no specific criteria cited, no section number, no IMR notice. The plan must reissue a compliant denial notice before the member can meaningfully exercise appeal rights.
genuine_tension: Clinical criteria clearly not met — this is a legitimate denial on the merits. But the denial notice violates CHSC 1374.31(b) on multiple grounds. A single-pass system reads the clinical record and upholds. A system applying the full regulatory framework catches the procedural defect. The correct disposition is not a binary overturn/uphold — it is a remand requiring a compliant denial notice.

determination:
HEALTHFIRST HEALTH PLAN
APPEAL DETERMINATION REPORT

Date: November 14, 2024
Case ID: PA-2024-C001
Member Name: Frances Kim
Member ID: M-990011
Plan: HealthFirst PPO Gold — Group Plan 77441
State of Residence: California
Requested Procedure: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C5-C6, one level (CPT 22551)
Requesting Physician: Dr. Robert Adams, MD — Neurosurgery, UCSF Medical Center
Facility: UCSF Medical Center
Prior Authorization Denial Date: October 30, 2024
Denial Reviewer: Dr. Alan Foster, MD (Initial Review)
Appeal Date: November 12, 2024

DISPOSITION: OVERTURNED (Prior Authorization Approved)

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The prior authorization denial for a single-level Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at C5-C6 (CPT 22551) is OVERTURNED. 

The initial denial was based on a mechanical application of HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024, citing that the member failed to complete the standard 6-week physical therapy (PT) requirement (completing 5 weeks) and that the "Myelopathy Exception" did not apply due to the absence of imaging-confirmed cord compression or signal change on MRI. 

Upon comprehensive clinical and regulatory review, this determination finds that:
1. The member has established clinical cervical myelopathy, supported by five objective upper motor neuron (UMN) signs on examination and correlating MRI findings of a C5-C6 disc herniation with mild cord contact.
2. Under CC-SPINE-2024 Exception 2.2(A) (Myelopathy Pathway), the PT requirement is reduced to 4 weeks. The member's completion of 5 weeks of PT (15 sessions) fully satisfies this requirement.
3. While the member did not complete the plan's internal pharmacotherapy requirement under Section 2.2(b) (completing only a 10-day Methylprednisolone trial instead of the required 4 weeks), California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.32 mandates that medical necessity determinations be governed by generally accepted standards of medical practice rather than restrictive internal plan criteria.
4. Under generally accepted clinical standards (AANS/CNS, NASS, AO Spine), a 4-week trial of oral corticosteroids is clinically contraindicated due to systemic toxicity risks, and conservative pharmacotherapy is ineffective for established clinical myelopathy. Delaying surgery to complete an unsafe and ineffective drug trial violates clinical standards and risks irreversible neurological deterioration.
5. While Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) All-Plan Letter APL 22-014 does not apply as a mandatory waiver in this case due to the absence of measurable cord compression or myelomalacia on MRI, the denial is overturned independently under CHSC § 1374.32 based on clinical standards.

Accordingly, the requested surgical intervention is medically necessary and is hereby approved.

II. CLINICAL PRESENTATION AND RECORD REVIEW
The clinical record for Frances Kim, a 58-year-old female, demonstrates the following:
- Presenting Diagnosis: Suspected cervical myelopathy — imaging-negative UMN syndrome (Clinical Record).
- Neurological Examination (September 5, 2024): Documented by Dr. Robert Adams, MD, demonstrating five objective upper motor neuron (UMN) signs:
  1. Positive Hoffman sign bilaterally.
  2. Hyperreflexia in bilateral upper extremities.
  3. Sustained clonus at bilateral ankles (3 beats).
  4. Positive finger escape sign.
  5. Mildly wide-based gait.
  The patient denies lower extremity symptoms (Clinical Record).
- Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) (September 1, 2024): Demonstrates a C5-C6 disc herniation with mild cord contact. The radiologist's note states: "Cord contact is present but not quantifiable as compression on standard sequences. No measurable cord compression. No T2 signal change. No myelomalacia." (Clinical Record).
- Physical Therapy (PT) Summary: Completed 5 weeks of supervised PT (15 sessions) under a myelopathy protocol. The treating physician halted PT prior to the standard 6 weeks, citing concerns over neurological safety and myelopathy progression. The PT notes indicate that the member's neurological signs remained unchanged, representing a clinical functional plateau (Clinical Record).
- Pharmacotherapy History:
  1. Baclofen 5mg TID for 2 months (muscle relaxant), resulting in minimal spasticity relief (Clinical Record).
  2. Methylprednisolone taper for 10 days (oral corticosteroid), resulting in no improvement in UMN signs (Clinical Record).

III. ANALYSIS OF PLAN CRITERIA AND FACTUAL GAPS
Under HealthFirst Clinical Coverage Criteria CC-SPINE-2024:
- Section 2.1(b) requires a confirmed diagnosis of cervical myelopathy, defined as "spinal cord compression with myelopathic symptoms (gait disturbance, bilateral upper extremity weakness, hyperreflexia, positive Hoffman sign, bowel/bladder dysfunction)."
- Section 2.2(a) requires a minimum of 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy.
- Section 2.2(b) requires a trial of at least two pharmacotherapy agents (NSAIDs, muscle relaxants, neuropathic agents, or oral corticosteroids) for a minimum of 4 weeks each.
- Exception 2.2(A) (Myelopathy Pathway) modifies these requirements for members with confirmed cervical myelopathy: the PT requirement is reduced to 4 weeks, the interventional treatment requirement (2.2(c)) is waived, but the "Pharmacotherapy requirement (2.2(b)) remains in full."

Factual Compliance Assessment:
1. Physical Therapy: The member completed 5 weeks of PT. Under the standard pathway, this is non-compliant (6 weeks required). Under the Myelopathy Pathway (Exception 2.2(A)), this is fully compliant (4 weeks required).
2. Pharmacotherapy: The member completed a 2-month trial of Baclofen (compliant). However, the member's trial of Methylprednisolone was only 10 days. Under a strict, mechanical reading of Section 2.2(b), the member is non-compliant because the second agent was not trialed for the minimum 4-week duration, and Exception 2.2(A) explicitly states that the pharmacotherapy requirement remains in full.

IV. LEGAL AND CLINICAL JUSTIFICATION FOR OVERTURN
While the member technically failed to meet the plan's internal 4-week duration requirement for the second pharmacotherapy agent under Section 2.2(b), the plan's denial must be overturned because the internal criteria are more restrictive than generally accepted standards of medical practice, in violation of California law.

1. Statutory Override of Restrictive Plan Criteria (CHSC § 1374.32)
Under California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.32(a), a health plan's medical necessity determinations must be made in accordance with "generally accepted standards of medical practice" and must be "clinically appropriate, in terms of type, frequency, extent, site, and duration."
Crucially, CHSC § 1374.32(b) explicitly states: "The IMR standard does NOT require that the service be consistent with the plan's internal coverage criteria. If the service meets the standard in subdivision (a), the reviewer SHALL recommend approval regardless of whether the plan's internal criteria are more restrictive."
Therefore, the member's technical non-compliance with the plan's internal 4-week steroid trial requirement is not a valid ground for denial if that requirement is clinically inappropriate and inconsistent with generally accepted medical standards.

2. Clinical Inappropriateness and Safety Risks of a 4-Week Steroid Trial
The plan's requirement of a 4-week trial of oral corticosteroids (Section 2.2(b)) is clinically inappropriate and highly unsafe. According to standard pharmacological and clinical practice, oral corticosteroids (such as Methylprednisolone) are prescribed as short-term tapers (typically 5 to 10 days) to treat acute inflammatory flares. Prolonged continuous use of oral steroids for 4 weeks is clinically contraindicated due to severe systemic risks, including:
- Adrenal suppression and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis dysfunction.
- Avascular necrosis of the femoral head.
- Severe hyperglycemia, hypertension, and immunosuppression.
Requiring a patient to undergo an unsafe, clinically contraindicated 4-week course of oral steroids to satisfy an administrative coverage criterion violates the clinical appropriateness standard of CHSC § 1374.32(a)(2).

3. Inefficacy of Pharmacotherapy and Risk of Neurological Delay in Myelopathy
Generally accepted clinical guidelines from major spine societies, including the AANS/CNS Joint Section on Disorders of the Spine (2023), the North American Spine Society (NASS, 2020), and AO Spine International (2021), establish that cervical myelopathy is a structural, mechanical compression of the spinal cord.
- Inefficacy: Pharmacotherapy (including muscle relaxants and steroids) has no clinical efficacy in reversing mechanical spinal cord compression or resolving objective upper motor neuron deficits (Clinical Reference Summary Section 1.1 & 5).
- Risk of Delay: Delaying surgical decompression to complete ineffective conservative treatments poses a severe risk of irreversible spinal cord injury. Prospective clinical studies demonstrate that each month of delay in surgical treatment for established myelopathy is associated with a decreased likelihood of neurological recovery (Clinical Reference Summary Section 2.3).
- Clinical Guidelines: The AO Spine Clinical Practice Guideline (2021) states: "There is no high-quality evidence supporting a mandatory course of physical therapy [or conservative treatment] prior to surgical intervention for patients with moderate to severe cervical myelopathy. Delaying surgery in such patients... is not supported by the evidence and may result in neurological deterioration." (Clinical Reference Summary Section 2.1).
Therefore, requiring a 4-week trial of an ineffective medication in a patient with established, progressive neurological signs is clinically contraindicated and inconsistent with generally accepted standards of medical practice.

4. Establishment of Clinical Myelopathy Notwithstanding MRI Findings
The plan's initial reviewer asserted that upper motor neuron signs are not conclusive for myelopathy in the absence of imaging-confirmed cord compression. This assertion is clinically incorrect.
According to the AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023), cervical myelopathy is primarily a clinical diagnosis established by the presence of objective upper motor neuron signs on physical examination. "Imaging-negative myelopathy" is a well-recognized clinical entity where clinical signs of spinal cord dysfunction precede gross structural changes visible on standard MRI sequences (Clinical Reference Summary Section 1.1).
Frances Kim exhibits five distinct, objective UMN signs (bilateral Hoffman, hyperreflexia, sustained ankle clonus, positive finger escape, and wide-based gait) with correlating structural pathology (C5-C6 disc herniation with mild cord contact). This clinical presentation establishes a definitive diagnosis of cervical myelopathy under generally accepted medical standards, satisfying CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.1(b) and triggering the Myelopathy Pathway.

5. Explicit Clarification on DMHC All-Plan Letter APL 22-014
We explicitly acknowledge that DMHC All-Plan Letter APL 22-014 does not apply as a mandatory waiver in this specific case. APL 22-014 Section II.1 and II.2 restrict its mandatory conservative treatment waivers to cases of "cervical myelopathy with objective evidence of cord compression and myelomalacia on MRI." Because Frances Kim's MRI explicitly noted "no measurable cord compression" and "no myelomalacia," the regulatory mandate of APL 22-014 is not triggered.
However, the plan's internal criteria remain fully subject to CHSC § 1374.32. The denial is overturned based on the statutory standard of CHSC § 1374.32 and generally accepted standards of medical practice, which operate independently of APL 22-014.

V. CONCLUSION AND APPROVAL
The requested Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C5-C6 (CPT 22551) is medically necessary under California Health & Safety Code § 1374.32 and generally accepted standards of medical practice.

The member has established clinical cervical myelopathy with objective neurological deficits. The physical therapy requirement has been met (5 weeks completed, exceeding the 4-week myelopathy pathway requirement). The plan's 4-week oral steroid trial requirement is clinically contraindicated, unsafe, and ineffective for this structural condition. Delaying surgery to complete this trial violates clinical standards and risks permanent neurological harm.

The prior authorization denial is OVERTURNED, and the procedure is APPROVED.

Authorized Signature:
Medical Director, Appeal Review Division
HealthFirst Health Plan (California Licensed Physician)
ground_truth_answer: OVERTURN — Under CHSC 1374.32, generally accepted medical standards govern. Clinical myelopathy is established by multiple positive UMN signs (bilateral Hoffman, bilateral hyperreflexia, sustained bilateral clonus) with imaging correlation (mild cord contact). The plan cannot require imaging-confirmed compression when accepted clinical standards recognize UMN-sign diagnosis. 5 weeks PT meets the 4-week myelopathy pathway. Route GATE given diagnostic ambiguity.
genuine_tension: The plan's definition of myelopathy implicitly requires imaging confirmation. The clinical standard recognizes imaging-negative myelopathy based on UMN signs. Member has multiple positive UMN signs and mild cord contact. The question is whether CHSC 1374.32 requires accepting the clinical definition of myelopathy or whether the plan's imaging requirement is a permissible restriction.

determination:
**APPEAL DETERMINATION: OVERTURN**

**CASE ID:** PA-2024-D002
**MEMBER:** Michael Green, M-445577
**PROCEDURE:** ACDF C5-C6, one level (CPT 22551)
**REVIEW DATE:** 2024-11-15

**SUMMARY OF DENIAL:**
The initial prior authorization request for ACDF C5-C6 for Michael Green was denied on 2024-11-08 with reason code MED-003, stating "Member does not meet criteria for requested procedure under plan policy." The denial notice referenced an attached criteria document, but no document was provided, nor was an Independent Medical Review (IMR) notice included.

**APPEAL BASIS:**
The appeal cites procedural defects (no criteria document attached, IMR notice missing) and the member's inability to evaluate the denial without the applied criteria.

**CLINICAL PRESENTATION REVIEW:**
Mr. Green presents with cervical radiculopathy at C5-C6 with functional impairment.
*   **Imaging (MRI):** C5-C6 large disc herniation, moderate left C6 nerve root compression. Critically, there is *no cord contact* and no mention of myelomalacia.
*   **Neurological Exam:** Left C6 dermatomal numbness, diminished left bicep reflex, and 4/5 left bicep weakness. These are classic radicular findings.
*   **Conservative Treatment:**
    *   **Physical Therapy:** 7 weeks (21 sessions) completed, with documentation of a functional plateau at week 6, and persistent radicular symptoms.
    *   **Pharmacotherapy:** Gabapentin 600mg TID for 4 months (partial relief) and Naproxen 500mg BID for 3 months (inadequate).
    *   **Interventional:** Left C6 epidural steroid injection with 40% relief, which returned to baseline in 3 weeks.

**KEY FINDINGS AND APPLICATION OF HIERARCHY:**

1.  **Procedural Adequacy of Denial (State Law – CHSC § 1374.31(b)):**
    *   The denial notice is procedurally defective. It failed to include the specific clinical criteria applied (by not attaching the referenced criteria document) and did not include the required IMR notice.
    *   **CHSC § 1374.31(b) states:** "A denial notice that fails to specify the clinical criteria applied or the specific clinical reason for the denial is DEFECTIVE and shall be treated as if no denial was issued for purposes of appeal timelines."
    *   **Conclusion:** This procedural defect alone is grounds for overturning the denial.

2.  **Application of Plan Criteria (HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024):**
    *   **Diagnosis (2.1a/c):** Mr. Green has a confirmed diagnosis of cervical radiculopathy (2.1a) with nerve root compression and symptoms, and a cervical disc herniation with objective neurological deficit (2.1c). MRI supports structural pathology. **CRITERIA MET.**
    *   **Conservative Treatment (2.2):**
        *   **Physical Therapy (2.2a):** Requires "minimum 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy with documented functional outcomes." Mr. Green completed 7 weeks of PT, and notes document a functional plateau at week 6. **CRITERIA MET.**
        *   **Pharmacotherapy (2.2b):** Requires "at least two... for minimum 4 weeks each." Mr. Green had Gabapentin for 4 months and Naproxen for 3 months. **CRITERIA MET.**
        *   **Interventional (2.2c):** Requires "one of the following." Mr. Green received a Left C6 epidural. **CRITERIA MET.**
    *   **Imaging Requirement (2.3):** Current MRI (2024-09-20) demonstrates pathology consistent with symptoms. **CRITERIA MET.**
    *   **Myelopathy Exception (2.2(A)):** This exception does *not* apply. Mr. Green's clinical presentation is clearly cervical radiculopathy, not myelopathy. The plan's criteria explicitly state this exception applies "only when myelopathy is the PRIMARY diagnosis."
    *   **Conclusion:** Contrary to the denial reason, Mr. Green appears to meet *all* of HealthFirst's stated clinical coverage criteria for CPT 22551 for cervical radiculopathy. The plan's denial based on "Member does not meet criteria" is unsubstantiated by its own policy when properly applied to the clinical facts.

3.  **Application of State Law – Physical Therapy Requirement (CIC § 10169.5):**
    *   Even if the plan were to imply the 7 weeks of PT was insufficient, **CIC § 10169.5(a)(2) states:** "A health insurer... shall not condition approval of a surgical procedure on completion of physical therapy where... The member has completed a course of physical therapy and the treating physician documents that the member reached a functional plateau without adequate resolution of symptoms."
    *   The clinical record explicitly states: "PT notes document plateau at week 6. Radicular symptoms persist."
    *   **Conclusion:** State law dictates that the plan cannot require further PT once a functional plateau has been reached, which is documented here. The PT requirement has been satisfied per state law.

4.  **Application of Clinical Standard (AANS/CNS 2023, NASS 2020):**
    *   The clinical documentation confirms cervical radiculopathy. Conservative treatment for radiculopathy typically involves 6-12 weeks of non-operative management.
    *   **AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023), Section 3.1, TIER 2 (Reasonable Indication):** "Radiculopathy with persistent symptoms after 6-12 weeks conservative tx" and "Significant functional impairment not responding to conservative care."
    *   Mr. Green has completed 7 weeks of PT, 4 months of pharmacotherapy, and an interventional procedure, with persistent radicular symptoms (numbness, weakness 4/5) and documented plateau. This aligns with the clinical standard for surgical intervention for persistent cervical radiculopathy after failed conservative management.
    *   **DMHC APL 22-014 and Myelopathy Clinical Criteria:** These guidelines and clinical standards concerning myelopathy, myelomalacia, and urgent treatment *do not apply* to this case, as Mr. Green has radiculopathy without evidence of spinal cord compression or myelomalacia. The distinction between myelopathy and radiculopathy is critical, and the evidence base for conservative treatment differs significantly.
    *   **Conclusion:** The requested procedure is consistent with generally accepted standards of medical practice for cervical radiculopathy failing conservative treatment.

**CONFLICT RESOLUTION & DISPOSITION:**

The plan's denial is fatally flawed due to multiple reasons:
1.  **Procedural Defects:** The denial notice failed to provide the specific criteria applied and the IMR notice, violating CHSC § 1374.31(b). This alone is sufficient grounds for overturn. (State Law > Plan Criteria).
2.  **Incorrect Application of Plan Criteria:** Upon review, the member demonstrably meets all of HealthFirst's published criteria for ACDF for cervical radiculopathy, including the specified conservative treatment requirements (7 weeks PT, two pharmacotherapy agents, one interventional procedure). The plan's stated reason for denial ("Member does not meet criteria") is not supported by the facts and its own policy.
3.  **State Law Override on PT:** Even if the plan were to have an unstated or more stringent interpretation of its PT requirement, state law (CIC § 10169.5) explicitly prohibits denial based on PT duration when a functional plateau has been reached, which is documented in Mr. Green's case. (State Law > Plan Criteria).
4.  **Clinical Standards:** The service is consistent with generally accepted clinical standards for radiculopathy requiring surgery after a trial of conservative care. (Clinical Standard > Plan Criteria).

Therefore, based on the three-source hierarchy (State law > Clinical standard > Plan criteria), the denial by HealthFirst is not supported.

**DETERMINATION:**
**OVERTURN** the denial.

**WARRANT:**
The denial is OVERTURNED due to significant procedural defects, the member meeting all applicable plan criteria, and the denial being inconsistent with California state law regarding physical therapy requirements and generally accepted clinical standards of medical practice. The denial notice was defective per CHSC § 1374.31(b) for failing to provide the specific criteria applied and the IMR notice. The member's clinical record demonstrates that all criteria outlined in HealthFirst CC-SPINE-2024 for radiculopathy, including the 6-week minimum for physical therapy (7 weeks completed with documented plateau), two pharmacotherapy agents (Gabapentin 4 months, Naproxen 3 months), and one interventional procedure (C6 epidural), have been met. Furthermore, California Insurance Code § 10169.5(a)(2) prohibits conditioning approval on further physical therapy once a functional plateau has been documented, which is the case here. Finally, the proposed surgery is consistent with TIER 2 indications of the AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023) for radiculopathy with persistent symptoms after conservative treatment. The myelopathy-specific exceptions and regulations are not applicable to this case, as Mr. Green's presentation is cervical radiculopathy.
ground_truth_answer: OVERTURN — on both clinical and procedural grounds. Clinically: all criteria met (7 weeks PT, 2 pharmacotherapy agents, injection, documented plateau, imaging correlation). Procedurally: denial notice violated CHSC 1374.31(b) — referenced attachment not provided, IMR notice absent. Both grounds should be documented.
genuine_tension: Unlike D001, this case meets criteria on the merits. The correct clinical outcome is overturn regardless of the procedural defect. A single-pass system reads the clinical record and correctly overturns. But the procedural defects should be documented in the determination so the plan is put on notice of the statutory violations.

2. **Naproxen 500mg BID** for 3 months (inadequate response). | **MET** | | **Section 2.2(c)** | At least one interventional treatment (epidural injection, medial branch block, or trigger point series). | **Left C6 epidural steroid injection** on 2024-10-28 (provided 40% temporary relief, returning to baseline in 3 weeks). | **MET** | | **Section 2.4** | Physician documentation of functional limitations, surgical risks/alternatives, and clinical rationale. | Dr. Sarah Kim, MD, documented cervical radiculopathy C5-C6 with functional impairment. | **MET** | * **Conclusion:** The member **fully satisfied every requirement** of the plan's standard conservative treatment pathway. The initial physician reviewer’s determination (MED-003) that the member "does not meet criteria" was a clear error of clinical oversight. ### Step 4: Statutory Override Analysis * **Statutory Authority:** California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5 * **Evaluation & Findings:** Physical therapy records document that the member reached a **functional plateau at week 6** of his 7-week course, with persistent radicular symptoms and objective 4/5 weakness remaining. Under **CIC § 10169.5(a)(2)**, a health insurer cannot condition the approval of a surgical procedure on the completion or continuation of physical therapy where: > *"The member has completed a course of physical therapy and the treating physician documents that the member reached a functional plateau without adequate resolution of symptoms."* Because a functional plateau was clinically documented by the physical therapist and treating physician at week 6, the plan is legally prohibited from demanding any further conservative physical therapy trials as a condition for surgical approval. ### Step 5: Clinical Standards & Medical Necessity Review * **Objective:** Evaluate if the surgery is medically necessary under generally accepted clinical standards. * **Clinical Guidelines Applied:** American Association of Neurological Surgeons / Congress of Neurological Surgeons (AANS/CNS) Joint Section Guidelines (2023 Update) and the North American Spine Society (NASS) Guidelines (2020). * **Clinical Standard Evaluation:** Under the AANS/CNS 2023 clinical guidelines, surgical intervention (ACDF) for cervical radiculopathy is highly indicated and classified as **Tier 2 (Reasonable Indication / Medically Necessary)** when a patient presents with: 1. Objective neurological deficits (motor weakness 4/5, reflex changes, and dermatomal sensory loss); 2. Correlating imaging showing nerve root compression (C5-C6 herniation compressing C6 root); and 3. Failure of a structured 6-to-12-week conservative care trial (including PT, oral pharmacotherapy, and epidural steroid injections). The member’s clinical history meets all of these parameters. Delaying surgical decompression in the presence of an active motor deficit (4/5 bicep weakness) and a documented failure of conservative therapy poses a high risk of permanent neurological deficit (muscle atrophy and chronic radicular neuropathy). Under **CHSC § 1374.32(b)**, because the procedure meets generally accepted clinical standards of medical practice, it must be approved regardless of any more restrictive plan interpretations. --- ## IV. CONCLUSION & APPEALS DECISION The initial medical necessity denial issued on 2024-11-08 under reason code MED-003 is **OVERTURNED**. * **Procedural Finding:** The plan’s denial was legally defective under **CHSC § 1374.31(b)** due to the omission of the referenced clinical criteria and the mandatory IMR notice. * **Substantive Finding:** The clinical record demonstrates complete compliance with HealthFirst's clinical coverage criteria **CC-SPINE-2024**. The member suffers from documented cervical radiculopathy with objective motor and sensory deficits that have failed to resolve after 7 weeks of physical therapy, multiple pharmacotherapy trials, and a targeted epidural steroid injection. * **Clinical Standard Finding:** The requested ACDF (CPT 22551) at C5-C6 is medically necessary, clinically appropriate, and indicated under generally accepted clinical standards of care to prevent permanent neurological injury. HealthFirst is ordered to issue an immediate authorization for CPT 22551 (ACDF C5-C6, one level) to be performed by Dr. Sarah Kim, MD, at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center. **Authorized by:** *Lead Medical Appeals Reviewer* *State of California Clinical Appeals Division* *Date of Determination: November 15, 2024*

Procedurally: denial notice violated CHSC 1374.31(b) — referenced attachment not provided, IMR notice absent. Both grounds should be documented.
